solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Calculating a reviewer dismissing debut will keep them unsettled

indicators.note: the shortened reviewer word holds the jumbled letters inside it, keeping them
the reviewer word loses its opening letter, its debut

parts.note: a critic reviews books, plays or films

indicators.note: letters of the word them are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic who has lost a first appearance keeps the newcomers on edge while doing sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'debut' is the reviewer's first letter, not a first night; 'unsettled' scrambles the letters to THME, which the shortened reviewer 'will keep' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic is the branch of mathematics concerned with working out sums, so it serves as a noun for calculating.

clue.text: Take on whole wearing legal action? Not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the combined word is dropped
the legal word has the total on it, wrapped around it as if worn

parts.note: a case is an action brought in a law court
a sum is a whole amount, the total

explanation.surface: Someone is being sued for everything they own and wonders whether to accept the challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' builds CASSUME; 'Not at first' then drops its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a role or responsibility is to take it on, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A summer date picked up after catching new lizard

indicators.note: the reversed letters take in the abbreviation for new
in a down entry, lifting the letters reverses them so they read upwards

parts.note: the first of August, written AUG I with a Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a summer outing and comes across an unusual reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: A AUG I reversed gives IGUAA, which takes N inside. 'picked up' only reverses because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, so lizard names its family as an example.

clue.text: Ulterior motive that could delay the meeting?

definitions.meaning: a secret purpose that someone keeps concealed behind an innocent front
if the list of business for a meeting were concealed, the meeting could not start on time

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: an agenda that has been tucked away somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock idiom for a concealed purpose, and literally a mislaid order of business for a meeting.

clue.text: Regret turning up zero money

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters are turned to read upwards

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
O looks like the figure nought

explanation.surface: Someone laments that their cash has come to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency of much of the European Union, an example of money.

clue.text: Including space on record of a provocative nature

parts.note: inc. is the usual short form of including
an en is a printer's unit of space
a diary is a daily written record

explanation.surface: A journal that includes a printing gap turns out to be inflammatory.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is half an em, a printer's measure of spacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Incendiary remarks are inflammatory, deliberately stirring up trouble, so the adjective fits a provocative nature.

clue.text: Response from energy company, bringing in source of heat

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the pair of abbreviations takes a letter into their middle
the word heat starts from its first letter, its source

explanation.surface: An energy supplier answers a question about heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives H, which goes between E and CO.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a reflected sound, and figuratively a reply or reaction, so it can stand for a response.

clue.text: Happen to find church without name when going round named church?

indicators.note: the nameless word encircles the abbreviation for the established church

parts.note: anon., short for anonymous, means without a name
CE is the Church of England, a church with a name

explanation.surface: A visitor stumbles on an anonymous chapel while touring a famous cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The two churches in the clue are different pieces: the first is the plain abbreviation, the 'named' one is the Church of England, which 'when going round' puts inside the nameless word.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance on something is the idiom for coming across it by luck.

clue.text: Party upset over million in damages? They're just a few items

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits above the next
in a down entry, upset means the word is turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: the abbreviation for million goes into the damage word

parts.note: dents are damage marks, so damages here is a verb or plural noun giving dents

explanation.surface: After a party gets out of hand, a million in compensation seems only small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the party word upwards in this down entry; 'in' places the million after the first letter of the damage word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover odds and ends, a small miscellany of things.

clue.text: Good place for running film music

parts.note: sound means solid, in good condition
a track is a course where athletes run

explanation.surface: A director praises a fine running track as a location for a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundtrack is the recorded music accompanying a movie.

clue.text: Name written in blue or yellowish-brown

indicators.note: the abbreviation is entered inside the word for melancholy

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad

explanation.surface: A name is inscribed in a choice between blue and tan paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a colour beside 'yellowish-brown', but it is the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand as a colour is the pale tan of beach grains.

clue.text: Remit implied by this honour?

parts.note: the word remit is a rearrangement of merit, so putting merit in a new order spells it

explanation.surface: The scope of a royal award is suggested by its own name.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: 'ORDER OF' read as an instruction rearranges MERIT into REMIT, the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of Merit is a British award given by the monarch for distinction in the arts, sciences or public life.

clue.text: Couple stepping back in little dance

indicators.note: a pair of letters, the last two, turn round within the small word

parts.note: minute means very small

explanation.surface: A pair of dancers retreat during a short dance.
explanation.walkthrough: MINUTE with its last two letters, TE, swapped to ET.
explanation.definitionFit: The minuet is a stately seventeenth-century court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Item for middle of play requiring space in middle of scenery

indicators.note: the expanse word goes inside the central letters
the central three letters of scenery are taken

parts.note: a tract is an expanse of land or space

explanation.surface: An interval act needs room among the stage sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes ENE from sCENEry's centre, and TRACT goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is an interlude or piece of music performed between the acts of a stage show.

clue.text: When a shock is even harder to bear?

definitions.text: When a shock is even harder to bear?

parts.words: When a shock is even harder to bear?
parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mop, and a day when it will not behave is miserable; also a day when bad news hits harder

explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' means a mass of hair, not a jolt; the phrase also means a day when everything goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a day when one's hair is unmanageable, and by extension a generally bad day.

clue.text: Poem excited ladies so in actor's words

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the role word

parts.note: a part is the role and lines an actor speaks

indicators.note: the letters of ladies so are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor recites verse that thrills the women in the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' looks like a description of the ladies but is the anagram signal; 'in' puts the scrambled letters inside the role.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise Lost is Milton's epic poem about the Fall of Man.

clue.text: German noble has tantrum over evidence of vandalism?

parts.note: Graf is the German title for a count
a fit of temper is a tantrum
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An aristocrat from Germany throws a fit about defaced property.
explanation.definitionFit: A graffito is a single piece of writing or drawing scrawled on a wall, often regarded as vandalism.

clue.text: One's broken up soldiers heading off into club?

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the club word

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub or bar

indicators.note: the soldiers' word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a force is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops, minus their leader, pile into a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves ORCE, and 'into' puts it before the club's last letter. 'broken up' in the definition means a marriage ended, not damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorcee is someone whose marriage has been dissolved, a person whose partnership has broken up.

clue.text: Storm? Provide protection from it, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to storm is to rage or make a great noise, as an excited crowd does
literally putting up a roof would keep out bad weather

explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the storm, so the second reading is literal building work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cheer or shout very loudly, or be furious, while literally it means lifting a roof into place.

clue.text: Suggestion taken up over her playing card game in Chicago?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
in a down entry the hint word is lifted to read upwards

parts.note: a cue is a hint or prompt

indicators.note: the letters of her are played about with into a new order

explanation.surface: A hint is taken by a card player at a game in Chicago.
explanation.walkthrough: CUE reversed gives EUC; 'playing' turns HER into HRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Euchre is a trick-taking card game long popular in the United States, hence the American setting.

clue.text: Wrap up copies in various forms

parts.note: sh is a command to be quiet, as in wrap up meaning shut up
to ape someone is to copy them

explanation.surface: Someone wraps up duplicates of a document in several formats.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapes are outlines or configurations, the varied forms that objects take.

clue.text: Fifty tucking into meat, perhaps flambé, visible in the dark

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the word for meat

parts.note: meat in its old sense means food in general
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a flambé dish is set alight, so lit is an example

explanation.surface: A diner eats a flaming dessert that glows in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' in its old sense of food, as in 'meat and drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Floodlit means lit by powerful lamps, so it can be seen after nightfall.

clue.text: Article with sentimentality about British raid

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the gooey word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: mush is sloppy sentimentality

explanation.surface: A newspaper item gushes sentimentally about a British attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack from hiding, a kind of raid.

clue.text: Tight spot, trouble initially appearing in three directions

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the compass points

parts.note: S, E and W are compass points: south, east, west

indicators.note: only the first letter of trouble is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is in a fix, with trouble coming at them from three sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew is an idiom for being in a state of anxious difficulty.

clue.text: First person from Germany to go round North Island

indicators.note: the German pronoun surrounds the abbreviation for north

parts.note: ich is German for I, the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A German traveller is the first to sail around an island in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' is grammar, not the earliest visitor. Inch is a Scottish word for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch, from Gaelic innis, names small islands in Scotland and Ireland, as in Inchcolm.

clue.text: Senior role in priesthood (I should replace one old, doddery)

indicators.note: the letters totter about into a new order
the letter I takes the place of one O in the church word

explanation.surface: An elderly priest is to be replaced by someone younger in the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIESTHOOD with one O swapped for I gives PRIESTHIOD, which 'doddery' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorship is the post of editor, a senior position on a publication.

clue.text: Ordinary outlet for fumes more than enough for this kitchen fixture

indicators.note: the combined letters are one too many for the answer, so the last is dropped

parts.note: a vent lets smoke and gas escape

explanation.surface: A plain extractor is overkill for this piece of kitchen equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: O plus VENT is one letter too long; 'more than enough' drops the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is a built-in cooking appliance, a standard fixture of a kitchen.

clue.text: Gloomy tree having special quality in curious sense, one observes

indicators.note: the tree and quality go inside the rearranged letters
the letters of sense are put into an odd order

parts.note: the yew is a dark tree associated with churchyards
it means sex appeal or a special something

explanation.surface: A dark tree with a strange aura seems to watch people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges SENSE to ENESS, which holds YEWIT after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is a person who sees an event take place, someone who observes it.
